iterations.narrative:
**Narrative**

The differential metabolite list is strikingly enriched for the **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism** pathway (KEGG map00590; SMP00075), which returned the highest fold-enrichment (735-fold) with an FDR of 0.0 across six of the seven input compounds. Six metabolites — arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, 11,12,15-THETA, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 — all map to this pathway, identifying it as the dominant affected system. The lone outlier, CDP (C00112), is a nucleotide intermediate unrelated to eicosanoid biology and likely reflects a separate, unconnected perturbation.

**Key driver compounds and directional relationships.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the obligate upstream precursor. KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms that arachidonic acid is directly connected (2 hops) to leukotriene A4 (C00909) via 5-HPETE (C05356), establishing the 5-lipoxygenase branch. Arachidonic acid is also upstream of 15-HETE (C04742) via an intermediate epoxide (C05966), confirming a second functional arm of the pathway activated in the treatment group.

**Biological significance.** These changes collectively indicate a robust activation of the arachidonic acid cascade, engaging both the lipoxygenase (leukotriene and HETE) and cyclooxygenase (15-deoxy-PGJ2) branches. Elevated leukotriene A4 and 5-HETE are hallmarks of inflammatory cell recruitment and bronchoconstriction. The presence of 15-HETE and 11,12,15-THETA (a maresin/THETA-series mediator precursor) points toward specialized pro-resolving lipid mediator production. CDP elevation is mechanistically disconnected; its biological context requires independent investigation. These findings are consistent with an inflammatory or pro-resolving stimulus that broadly Reprograms the arachidonic acid metabolome.

**Narrative**

The differential metabolite list is enriched for the **Leukotriene C4 Synthesis Deficiency** pathway (SMP00353, FDR 0.0, fold-enrichment 735.3) and the **Rofecoxib Action Pathway** (SMP00087, FDR 0.0, fold-enrichment 735.3), both ranked top-1 among SMPDB pathways. Six compounds — 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, arachidonic acid, 11,12,15-THETA, and leukotriene A4 — map to these pathways, identifying eicosanoid signalling as the dominant affected system. The lone outlier, CDP (C00112), maps to nucleotide metabolism pathways and does not belong to the enriched eicosanoid clusters.

**Key driver compounds and directional relationships.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the obligate upstream precursor. KEGG reaction-graph analysis confirms that arachidonic acid is directly connected (2 hops) to leukotriene A4 (C00909) via 5-HPETE (C05356), establishing the 5-lipoxygenase branch of the leukotriene pathway. This connection is bidirectional, consistent with the known reversibility of this enzymatic step.

**Biological significance.** These changes indicate activation of the eicosanoid cascade, engaging both the lipoxygenase (leukotriene A4 and HETE mediators) and cyclooxygenase (15-deoxy-PGJ2) branches. Elevated leukotriene A4 and 5-HETE are hallmarks of inflammatory cell recruitment. CDP elevation reflects a separate, unrelated metabolic perturbation in nucleotide biochemistry. Together, the findings are consistent with an inflammatory or pharmacological stimulus that broadly reprograms eicosanoid signalling.

**Limitations.** The RaMP-DB enrichment analysis did not return a standalone "Arachidonic Acid Metabolism" entry; instead, enriched pathways are annotated as SMPDB drug-action and deficiency contexts. Directional upstream/downstream relationships are supported only for the arachidonic acid → leukotriene A4 pair; other compound relationships were not verified in this analysis.
